bihar_raw_news.title: Delhi- Bihar Chhath Travel Gets 77 Subsidised Buses from Anand Vihar - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Delhi-Bihar Chhath Travel Gets 77 Subsidised Buses from Anand Vihar Breaking News Delhi-Bihar Chhath Travel Gets 77 Subsidised Buses from Anand Vihar By Maria Dsouza November 13, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Delhi and Bihar have launched 77 inter-state buses from Anand Vihar Bus Terminal to help passengers travel home for Chhath at subsidised fares, with services connecting five Bihar divisions and offering both air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned options. The arrangement was announced by Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Singh, who said the services were introduced through a Memorandum of Understanding approved by the two state governments. The buses are intended to support residents of Bihar and Poorvanchal living in Delhi during the seasonal travel rush. “Chhath Puja holds immense cultural and emotional significance for lakhs of people from Bihar and Poorvanchal residing in Delhi,” Singh said. He added that the governments were working together to help passengers travel safely and affordably, describing the additional services and subsidised fares as a step towards improving access to public transport during the festival. The 77 buses will serve five Bihar divisions. Muzaffarpur will receive the largest allocation with 36 buses, followed by Patna with 13, Purnea with 12, Gaya Ji with 10 and Darbhanga with six buses. Passengers will be able to choose from non-AC seater, non-AC sleeper, AC seater and AC sleeper services. According to the minister, festival fare reductions will range from Rs 134 to Rs 1,028, depending on the route and the category of bus selected. The initiative comes as Delhi’s transport network faces increased demand from passengers travelling to Bihar for Chhath. By adding inter-state services at Anand Vihar, the arrangement provides an organised public transport option for travellers who may otherwise depend on limited or higher-priced services during the festive period. Officials said the programme could also increase revenue for the Delhi Transport Corporation. The agreement provides for mutual recognition of tickets issued in Delhi and Bihar, allowing tickets purchased in either state to be accepted under the arrangement. The participating services will have to meet specified operational and safety conditions. Officials said only BS-VI compliant CNG buses and electric buses would be permitted. The buses will also be required to have vehicle location-tracking devices and emergency buttons. The agreement is valid for 10 years, subject to applicable legal provisions. The two governments have described the arrangement as a measure to strengthen interstate public transport connectivity while easing the festive travel rush. The immediate services are being operated from Anand Vihar across the five identified Bihar divisions. national_raw_news.title: New Tractor Plant in UP’s Jewar to Generate 1,200 Direct Jobs
national_raw_news.content: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday virtually laid the foundation stone for a tractor manufacturing plant in the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) area of Jewar, with the project expected to generate around 1,200 direct jobs. The state-of-the-art facility, to be set up by CNH Industrial on 100 acres in Sector 8 of the YEIDA region, involves an estimated investment of Rs 1,200 crore. Besides direct employment, the project is expected to create a significant number of indirect jobs. Speaking at the event, Adityanath said Jewar was emerging as one of India’s prominent investment destinations. With the development of the Noida International Airport and several industrial projects in the YEIDA region, the area is poised to become a major industrial, economic and logistics hub, he said. The chief minister attributed the rise in investments to improvements in the state’s law-and-order situation and the government’s zero-tolerance policy towards crime. He also credited the support of local farmers and public representatives for opening up new avenues of development in the region. Referring to the state’s enforcement measures against illegal activities, Adityanath said the bulldozer had become a “brand of Uttar Pradesh”. He added that manufacturing products such as bulldozers and tractors in the state would help meet growing demand in domestic and international markets. Under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Uttar Pradesh has received investment proposals worth more than Rs 50 lakh crore over the past nine-and-a-half years, he said. Of these, investments worth nearly Rs 15 lakh crore have materialised, while proposals worth Rs 7.5 lakh crore are expected to reach the ground-breaking stage soon. Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh had moved beyond the category of underdeveloped states and emerged as one of the country’s three largest economies, while pursuing the target of becoming a $1 trillion economy. Highlighting the state’s industrial expansion, he said the number of factories had increased from 14,000 to 35,000, while the number of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) had reached one crore. The number of startups had also grown from 120 to 25,000, he added. The chief minister said Uttar Pradesh had established itself in Ease of Doing Business, “Fearless Business” and “Trust of Doing Business”, and ranked first in the country in deregulation. He also highlighted several projects coming up in the Jewar and YEIDA region, including the HCL-Foxconn semiconductor plant, Medical Device Park, Toy Park, MSME Park and multiple data centre projects. The state was also creating opportunities in emerging sectors such as information technology, semiconductors, cybersecurity, robotics and agritech, Adityanath said. Through collaborations with companies including Tata, Samsung, Microsoft, IBM, Infosys and HCL, the government was providing skill development training to young people to prepare an industry-ready workforce, he added. The CNH Industrial facility is expected to provide fresh impetus to the state’s agricultural machinery and tractor manufacturing sector, the chief minister said. Uttar Pradesh accounts for around 18.5 per cent of India’s tractor market, and the project would support industrial growth while benefiting the local economy and agriculture sector, he added. (IANS inputs)
